headline: Eliminate one row or column at a corner
statement: Determine whether target occurs in a rectangular matrix sorted in nondecreasing order both left-to-right within each row and top-to-bottom within each column.
constraints: Rows and columns are sorted in nondecreasing order
intuition: At the top-right corner, all values to the left are smaller and all values below are larger. If the corner is too big, its whole column can be removed; if too small, its whole row can be removed.
approach: Begin at row zero and the final column.
Return true on equality; move left when the value is above target.
Otherwise move down; return false when the position exits the matrix.
correctness: The unsearched candidates form a bottom-left rectangle. A too-large corner proves every value beneath it in the same column is too large. A too-small corner proves every value to its left in the row is too small. Removing these cannot remove target.
bruteForce: Inspect every cell in O(mn) time, or binary-search each row in O(m log n).

complexity.explanation: Every move discards a row or column; coordinates are the only extra state.

pitfalls: Rows need not form a globally sorted flattened sequence.
Start at top-right or bottom-left, where the two directions differ.
Stop on either row or column boundary.
